title: A Lost Game From 1977 Is Playable Again
summary: Long before video games had pictures, they were made of words. You typed a command, and the game answered with a sentence. One of the first of those games was called Magic Caves. It came out in 1977, and it was lost for many years. This weekend, computer historians made it work on modern computers for the first time. The year 1977 also saw the famous game Zork. But Magic Caves stayed hidden. Its maker was John Burgess Trenholme, a physicist who studied at the California Institute of Technology. In his free time, he built Magic Caves on an early computer. In the game, you explore a set of magic caves. An old man warns you the rooms hold treasures, but also dangers. With only a lantern, you face new challenges each time. You try to get the highest score out of 2,800 points. Stuck? A wizard can help, but he charges 100 points. The game had been saved on a fan's hard drive in 1999, then forgotten. Computer historian Jason Dyer found it. He called it a 'missing link' to the games that came later.
why_it_matters: The games on your phone started with simple word games like this one.

background_read: The first video games had no pictures at all: players typed commands and the game answered with written descriptions.
Early games were often shared between engineers and hobbyists on university computers.
Many early games were lost because they were stored on old tapes and disks that were thrown away.
